official.deadline_note: One Australia Awards calendar covers all five MAP countries: applications opened 1 February 2026 (09:00 AEDT) and closed 30 April 2026 (14:00 AEST) for study commencing 2027. Thailand's MAP intake published the same dates. Applications and/or supporting documents received after the closing date will not be considered.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake (study commencing in 2027); DFAT runs one Australia Awards round per country per year
official.status_note: The published 2027 intake round opened 1 February 2026 and closed 30 April 2026. As at the verification date of 10 October 2026 that round has closed: the selection process runs after the closing date, shortlisted candidates are notified by mid-August 2026, and successful candidates are notified during 2026 for 2027 commencement. DFAT had not published dates for the next intake at the verification date.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full tuition fees. In the Policy Handbook this appears as 'Academic Fees - Paid by Australia Awards Section directly to the institution - Covers the course costs and all compulsory academic fees that apply to international students.'
official.funding_period: per year (A$99.26 per day, paid fortnightly)
benefits: Full tuition fees - academic fees paid directly to the institution, covering the course costs and all compulsory academic fees that apply to international students
Return air travel - payment of a single return, economy class airfare to and from Australia, via the most direct route
Establishment allowance - a one-off payment of A$5,000 towards expenses such as rental bonds, textbooks, study materials, additional medical insurance and home contents insurance
Contribution to Living Expenses (CLE) - a fortnightly payment paid at a rate determined by DFAT; from 1 January 2026 the CLE rate is A$99.26 per day, or approximately A$36,230 per annum

Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the duration of the award (award holder only), plus payment of visa processing and medical checks necessary for the Student visa (subclass 500), and a compulsory 4-6 week Introductory Academic Program with a A$2,500 DFAT contribution

Exclusive access to the Mekong-Leaders Network, an on-award enrichment program of activities, events and development opportunities fostering collaboration and enduring connections between AA-MAP scholars across the Mekong subregion
eligibility: Citizen of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos or Myanmar, undertaking a Master's by research or Master's by coursework qualification at an Australian tertiary institution

The choice of study or research must fall within one of the MAP thematic areas: water security, climate action, combatting transnational crime, economic resilience and subregional integration, or gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI)

Applicants must meet all general Australia Awards Scholarships eligibility requirements in the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook, plus the country-specific conditions of their own country profile

Cambodia: be a citizen of Cambodia with no dual or additional citizenship; be resident in Cambodia for the 24 months immediately prior to 30 April 2026 other than short absences related to employment, professional development or holidays; have at least 24 months' full-time (or part-time equivalent) work experience as at 30 April 2026

Myanmar: be a citizen and resident of Myanmar; have completed a Bachelor's degree; have at least four years of work experience; not already have a Master's degree in the same field; not already have or be enrolled in an international Master's degree. Laos and Thailand (Master's applicants): hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent and have a minimum of two years' work experience
Applications are strongly encouraged from women and people living with disability, people from ethnic minority groups and people living in provincial areas
requirements: Lodge a complete application online through OASIS before the closing date, using your full name exactly as it appears on your passport (no nicknames, shortened versions or abbreviations)
Applicants interested in becoming a MAP scholar should highlight their eligibility for a MAP-funded scholarship in their written application

Upload all supporting documents required by your country profile; the maximum document size is 2 MB per document, OASIS accepts only .doc, .docx, .rtf, .pdf, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .tiff, .png, .bmp and .txt files, and documents presented in any language other than English must be translated into English
Read the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook before applying; DFAT may revise and update it at any time without notice

AI may only be used for basic tasks such as spelling, grammar and organising ideas - it must not be used to write, improve or paraphrase any part of the application, and misuse may result in disqualification

Scholars must sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia and leave Australia for a minimum of two years after completing their scholarship; failure to do so results in a debt for the total accrued cost of the scholarship
documents: Certified copies of all official university degree certificates and all official university transcripts of results for complete and incomplete courses of study, including current study
Evidence of personal identification and date of birth (passport personal information pages, national ID card or birth certificate) - certified

Evidence or statement(s) from workplace(s) confirming position held, duration of employment and full-time or part-time status, dated and signed by the employer(s), sufficient to satisfy the work-experience eligibility requirement
Curriculum Vitae on the prescribed template available from the in-country Australia Awards office
Formal English language test result (certified) obtained after 1 January 2025

Master's by Research applicants: a minimum of two academic referee reports on the official referee report template, plus evidence of extensive correspondence with the proposed supervisor or faculty demonstrating in-principle support for the research topic
selection_criteria: Professional and personal qualities, and academic competence
Relevance of study to the MAP key thematic areas
Potential to contribute to joint solutions to current and emerging challenges in the Mekong subregion
Potential outcome, specifically the contribution to development outcomes in the applicant's own country, and professional and personal leadership attributes including relevant work experience
Applications are strongly encouraged from women and people living with disability, people from ethnic minority groups and people living in provincial areas
Applications are shortlisted after eligibility checking and the selection process includes an interview; only shortlisted candidates are contacted
coverage: Tuition: course costs and all compulsory academic fees that apply to international students, paid direct to the institution
Living costs: Contribution to Living Expenses of A$99.26 per day from 1 January 2026 (approximately A$36,230 per annum), paid fortnightly
Start-up costs: a one-off A$5,000 establishment allowance for rental bonds, textbooks, study materials and insurance
Travel: a single return economy class airfare to and from Australia via the most direct route, plus completion travel and reunion airfare for unaccompanied scholars
Health and visa costs: single Overseas Student Health Cover for the duration of the award (award holder only) and payment of visa processing and medical checks for the Student visa (subclass 500)

Academic extras: a compulsory 4-6 week Introductory Academic Program (A$2,500 DFAT contribution), supplementary academic support at A$500 every six months on scholarship, pre-course English fees if deemed necessary, and a fieldwork allowance for research students and coursework students with a compulsory fieldwork component
application_method: Check the opening and closing dates for your country of citizenship and select your country from the list of participating countries for specific eligibility, priority areas and how to apply
Register online in OASIS (oasis.dfat.gov.au) and answer the eligibility questions to obtain a unique registration number, username and password

Build a draft application - it can be edited until the designated closing date - and upload all supporting documents before submitting; OASIS experiences peak usage in the days leading up to the closing date
Citizens of Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar follow the same application procedure for the Australia Awards Scholarships for their country
Citizens of Thailand follow the Thailand Australia Awards intake information and apply for the MAP-funded scholarships for Thai citizens

If online submission is not possible, a hard-copy application form can be obtained from the in-country contact and must be received by the closing date (in Cambodia, hand delivered or mailed to the Australian Embassy, Phnom Penh)
official.application_route: Apply online through OASIS in your own country's Australia Awards round and flag MAP eligibility in the written application; Thai citizens apply through the Thailand Australia Awards intake, while Cambodian, Laotian, Myanmar and Vietnamese applicants use their standard country process.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos or Myanmar. Cambodia additionally requires Cambodian citizenship with no dual or additional citizenship and 24 months' residence in Cambodia immediately prior to the closing date; Myanmar requires the applicant to be a citizen and resident of Myanmar.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is for citizens of the five Mekong countries to study in Australia; applicants apply from their home country, not from within Australia.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The proposed Master's coursework or research must fall within one of the MAP thematic areas: water security; climate action; combatting transnational crime; economic resilience and subregional integration; or gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI). DFAT lists the eligible fields under each theme, and in Cambodia general management degrees such as a Master of Business Administration are excluded.
official.research_requirement: Master's by Research applicants must provide evidence (for example a letter or email) of extensive correspondence with the proposed supervisor or faculty, demonstrating serious progress on thesis development over a period of time and in-principle support for their research topic, plus a minimum of two academic referee reports.
official.duration: The minimum period necessary for the individual to complete the academic program specified by the Australian higher education institution, including any preparatory training.
official.description: MAP-funded scholarships give citizens of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar the opportunity to obtain a Master's by research or Master's by coursework qualification at an Australian tertiary institution in one of the partnership's thematic areas. Award benefits remain the same as the Australia Awards program, with the addition of exclusive access to the Mekong-Leaders Network on-award enrichment program. DFAT is providing an additional 30 Masters scholarships per year across the subregion under the Mekong-Australia Partnership.
official.region: Oceania - study at an Australian tertiary institution; applicants are citizens of the Mekong subregion
official.program_type: Australia Awards Scholarships - MAP-funded sub-programme, Master's by coursework or Master's by research
official.english_requirement: Set per country. Thailand: IELTS Academic overall at least 6.5 with no band less than 6.0, or internet-based TOEFL at least 84 with a minimum of 21 in all subtests, or PTE Academic overall 58 with no communicative skill score less than 50. Cambodia, Master's by coursework: IELTS Academic overall at least 6.0 with no band less than 5.5, or TOEFL at least 60, or PTE Academic 50; Master's by research and PhD: IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0, TOEFL 84 (minimum 21 in all subtests), or PTE 58 with no skill below 50. Vietnam: scores differ by employer sector (public sector 6.5 with test results optional at IELTS 5.0; NGOs and private sector 7.0 with results required at IELTS 6.0; international organisations 7.0 with results required at IELTS 6.5). Test results must be obtained after 1 January 2025; IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted for Australia Awards eligibility purposes but placement is subject to university acceptance. Selected awardees must still attain the prescribed score before the award is confirmed, with up to six months of funded English training available, and failure to reach it results in the provisional scholarship being withdrawn.

not_confirmed: A MAP-specific stipend figure: DFAT states that MAP-funded scholarship benefits 'remain the same as the Australia Awards program', so the A$99.26 per day CLE rate is the standard Australia Awards rate rather than a MAP-only published amount
A single MAP-wide English requirement: minimum scores are published per country and, in Vietnam, by employer sector
A fixed programme duration: DFAT publishes only the minimum period necessary to complete the specified academic programme
Per-country MAP quotas: DFAT publishes only 'an additional 30 Masters scholarships per year' across the subregion, with no country breakdown
Dates for the next intake (study commencing 2028), which were not published as at the verification date
verification.notes: Checked DFAT's own pages: the Mekong-Australia Partnership scholarship page, the Australia Awards Scholarships benefits and how-to-apply pages, the opening and closing dates table, the Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam 2027 intake publications, and the June 2026 Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook, which is the source of the A$99.26 per day CLE rate, the A$5,000 establishment allowance and the A$2,500 Introductory Academic Program contribution.

applicant_utility.summary: MAP is the Mekong strand of the Australia Awards Scholarships, so you apply through your own country's normal annual Australia Awards round rather than a separate MAP window, and the money is the standard package: full tuition, a A$5,000 establishment allowance, a A$99.26-per-day living stipend, return airfares, health cover and visa costs. Your proposed course has to sit inside one of the five MAP thematic areas - water security, climate action, transnational crime, subregional economic integration or GEDSI - so choose your CRICOS course before you start writing and state the MAP link explicitly in the application. Thai citizens apply through the Thailand Australia Awards intake, while applicants in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam use their usual country process, and you may hold both a MAP and a standard Australia Awards application at the same time. The 2027 round closed on 30 April 2026, so the realistic target is the next annual intake, which DFAT had not yet dated at verification.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals in the five Mekong countries whose day job and proposed Master's study both line up with water security, climate action, transnational crime, subregional economic integration or GEDSI, and who can absorb two years away from work plus the two-year return-home condition.
application_readiness_checklist: Map your intended course to a named MAP thematic area and record its seven-digit CRICOS code before you draft anything - a course with no thematic anchor cannot be funded as MAP.
Book an English test early: results must be dated after 1 January 2025, and your final score after any funded English training still has to clear the bar or the provisional offer is withdrawn.
Collect certified copies of every degree certificate and every transcript, including incomplete and current study, because undeclared study is treated as potential fraud and bars future rounds.
Ask employers now for signed, dated statements covering position, duration and full-time or part-time status - generic HR letters are the most common documentary shortfall.
Open an OASIS account and save a draft as soon as the round opens, keeping each upload a single file under 2 MB in an accepted format.
For research applicants, start the supervisor email trail months ahead and commission the two academic referee reports on the official template in good time.
common_rejection_risks: The proposed course does not sit clearly inside a MAP thematic area, or the thematic link is only implied rather than argued in the written application.
Undeclared previous or current study - DFAT treats this as fraud, which voids the application and bars the applicant from future Australia Awards rounds.
An English shortfall after selection: the offer stays provisional, and failing to reach the prescribed score after up to six months of paid training means the award is withdrawn.
Missing certified transcripts, an untranslated document, or a CV that is not on the prescribed template, any of which makes an otherwise strong application ineligible.
Leaving the OASIS submission to the closing days of the April window, when portal congestion produces failed uploads that cannot be repaired after the deadline.
For research applicants, thin or late evidence of supervisor engagement - no in-principle support and no correspondence trail to show.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Dependants are entirely self-funded, since the Australian Government provides no financial support for them. Beyond the award you still carry ancillary medical costs excluded from basic OSHC such as dental, optical and physiotherapy, additional insurance, pre-existing conditions, and any income gap during the roughly three weeks of compulsory pre-departure training and up to six months of in-country English training, where the training stipend is modest - in Cambodia A$270-370 a month depending on location and employer sector.
document_audit: OASIS caps each document at 2 MB and accepts only .doc, .docx, .rtf, .pdf, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .tiff, .png, .bmp and .txt, so split or rescan long transcripts before upload.

Degree certificates, transcripts, proof of citizenship and English test results must be certified, while CVs and employer statements use the official templates, are not certified, and must still be signed and dated.
Documents in any language other than English need an English translation; certification of the translation is not required at application for Cambodia.
Your OASIS name must match your passport exactly - no nicknames, shortened forms or abbreviations - or your file will not reconcile with your identity documents.
English results must be dated after 1 January 2025, and IELTS One Skill Retake counts for Australia Awards eligibility but university placement remains at the institution's discretion.
alerts: The 2027 intake closed on 30 April 2026, so there is no live window at verification; DFAT runs one annual round per country and had not published the next cycle's dates.
You must hold only the citizenship of your MAP country - Cambodia explicitly excludes dual or additional citizenship, and Myanmar requires you to be both citizen and resident.
Residency and work-experience clocks run to the closing date, not the start of study: Cambodia requires 24 months of in-country residence and 24 months of work experience as at 30 April 2026.
You must leave Australia for at least two years after completing the scholarship, or you incur a debt to the Commonwealth for the total accrued cost of the award.
Only shortlisted applicants are contacted, typically by mid-August, so silence is normal - keep the email address in your OASIS profile active.

Course choice can be excluded outright: Cambodia states scholarships are not available for general management degrees such as a Master of Business Administration, while DFAT actively encourages applications from women, people with disability, ethnic minority groups and people living in provincial areas, with a support scheme available in some countries
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in OASIS, answer the eligibility questions, then build a draft with your CRICOS course preferences and upload every certified document under 2 MB; submit well before your country's closing date (14:00 AEST, 30 April 2026 for the 2027 round), after which nothing can be edited and assessment happens only once the round has closed.
